source.text: Ὅτε οὖν ἐξῆλθεν λέγει Ἰησοῦς· Νῦν ἐδοξάσθη ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, καὶ ὁ θεὸς ἐδοξάσθη ἐν αὐτῷ·

records.literal_gloss: When therefore he went out, says Jesus, "Now was glorified the Son of the Man, and the God was glorified in him;

en.L: So when he had gone out, Jesus says, "Now the Son of Man has been glorified, and God has been glorified in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: When Judas had gone out, Jesus said, "The Son of Man has now been glorified, and in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} God has been glorified.
en.R: After Judas left, Jesus said, "The time has come. Now the Son of Man is glorified, and God's glory is shown in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Cuando salió, dice Jesús: «Ahora ha sido glorificado el Hijo del Hombre, y Dios ha sido glorificado en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Cuando Judas salió, Jesús dijo: «Ahora ha sido glorificado el Hijo del Hombre, y en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} Dios ha sido glorificado.
es.R: Cuando Judas se fue, Jesús dijo: «Ha llegado el momento. Ahora el Hijo del Hombre es glorificado, y la gloria de Dios se muestra en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

sw.L: Basi alipotoka nje, Yesu anasema, "Sasa Mwana wa Adamu ametukuzwa, na Mungu ametukuzwa ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.B: Yuda alipokwisha kutoka, Yesu akasema, "Mwana wa Adamu ametukuzwa sasa, na ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} Mungu ametukuzwa.
sw.R: Baada ya Yuda kuondoka, Yesu akasema, "Wakati umefika. Sasa Mwana wa Adamu anatukuzwa, na utukufu wa Mungu unaonekana ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.

decisions.choice: When he had gone out: Judas's leaving (13:30) opens what follows
decisions.reason: "Therefore" ties these words to 13:30: Judas has taken the piece of bread and gone out into the night to betray Jesus. With the betrayer gone, Jesus speaks to the eleven alone. Here his farewell words to the disciples begin; they run on to his prayer in chapter 17 (13:31-17:26).

decisions.choice: has been glorified: a past tense for what is about to happen
alternatives: glorified already in his past ministry and signs only
a simple statement about the present moment
decisions.reason: The hour of the Son of Man's glorifying is his death, resurrection and return to the Father (12:23, 27-28; 17:1, 5). Judas's going out has set it in motion, so Jesus speaks of it as already done: it is that certain, and it has begun. "Now" marks this moment as the turning point. Verse 32 then speaks of the same glorifying in the future.

decisions.choice: God has been glorified in him: God's glory is shown in the Son and in what he does
alternatives: God is glorified by him, as an instrument only
decisions.reason: "In him" means in the Son's person and in his obedient work, above all his death. Jesus says the same in prayer: he has glorified the Father by finishing the work given him (17:4). The Father's glory and the Son's are bound together (12:28; 14:13).

decisions.choice: says (L); said (B, R); also verses 36, 37 and 38
decisions.reason: John often tells past events in the present tense ("says", "answers") to make a scene vivid. Literal keeps the present; Balanced and Readable use the past, as stories are normally told. This applies to every such verb in the passage ("says" in verses 36 and 37, "answers" in verse 38). "Answered" in verse 36 is already a past tense in Greek.

decisions.choice: Judas (B, R); The time has come, and God's glory is shown in him (R); has now been glorified ... in him God has been glorified (B)
alternatives: Now the Son of Man has been glorified (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the one who went out (13:30). Readable says plainly that the time has come and uses the present "is glorified", to show that the glorifying is happening now and is about to be completed (meaning decision m2); it says that God's glory "is shown" in the Son, which is what being glorified in him means (meaning decision m3). Balanced puts "in him" first to keep the stress on the Son.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal; pretérito at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in John: Literal keeps John's present ("dice", "ven"); Balanced and Readable use the pretérito. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: Judas (B, R); Ha llegado el momento (R)
decisions.reason: As in English; "momento" because "hora" is kept for the Greek word for hour.

source.text: εἰ ὁ θεὸς ἐδοξάσθη ἐν αὐτῷ, καὶ ὁ θεὸς δοξάσει αὐτὸν ἐν αὑτῷ, καὶ εὐθὺς δοξάσει αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: If the God was glorified in him, also the God will glorify him in himself, and at once will glorify him.

en.L: If God has been glorified in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, God will also glorify {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}, and will glorify {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} at once.
en.B: If God has been glorified in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, God will glorify {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} as well, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will do it without delay.
en.R: Since God has been glorified in the Son, God will also glorify the Son with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own glory. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will do it very soon.

es.L: Si Dios ha sido glorificado en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, Dios también lo glorificará en {{deity_pronoun:sí|Sí}} mismo, y enseguida lo glorificará.
es.B: Si Dios ha sido glorificado en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, Dios también lo glorificará en {{deity_pronoun:sí|Sí}} mismo, y lo hará sin demora.
es.R: Ya que Dios ha sido glorificado en el Hijo, Dios también glorificará al Hijo con su propia gloria. Y lo hará muy pronto.

sw.L: Ikiwa Mungu ametukuzwa ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, Mungu naye atamtukuza ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}, na atamtukuza mara moja.
sw.B: Ikiwa Mungu ametukuzwa ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, Mungu atamtukuza pia ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} atafanya hivyo bila kukawia.
sw.R: Kwa kuwa Mungu ametukuzwa ndani ya Mwana, Mungu atamtukuza Mwana kwa utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}. Na atafanya hivyo hivi karibuni sana.

decisions.choice: If God has been glorified in him (SBLGNT, included)
alternatives: the clause is left out (P66, Sinaiticus first hand, Vaticanus, Bezae and others)
decisions.reason: Several of the oldest manuscripts lack these words, among them Papyrus 66, the first hand of Codex Sinaiticus, Codex Vaticanus and Codex Bezae, with some others. Many manuscripts have them, among them Codex Alexandrinus and the corrector of Sinaiticus. A copyist's eye could easily jump from "in him" at the end of verse 31 to the same words here and leave the clause out; the clause could also have been added to link the two verses. The SBLGNT includes it, and the sense is not changed much either way. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: if: a condition taken as true (since)
alternatives: a real doubt whether God has been glorified
decisions.reason: The "if" picks up the statement Jesus has just made in verse 31; it reasons from it, not doubting it.

decisions.choice: in himself: in God himself, that is, in God's own glory
decisions.reason: The word for "himself" is the reflexive form in the SBLGNT, which normally points back to the subject of its clause, here God. The Son is then taken up into the Father's own glory, as Jesus prays in 17:5 to be glorified in the Father's presence with the glory he had with him before the world existed. The earliest manuscripts had no breathing marks, so the same letters could be read as "in him", meaning in the Son; then the Son's glory comes from within his own person. Both readings say that God will glorify the Son.

decisions.choice: at once: without delay, in the coming events
alternatives: at the end of the age
decisions.reason: The glorifying does not wait for a distant future. It comes within days, in the cross, the resurrection and his going to the Father (12:23; 17:1, 5).

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun on every pronoun, for God and for the Son
decisions.reason: Every pronoun in this verse refers to God or to the Son, so each one takes the setting, "himself" included, whichever of them it means (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: the Son; with his own glory; very soon
decisions.reason: Readable names the Son, so the reader can tell the two persons apart, and follows meaning decision m3 in saying "with his own glory" for "in himself". That is an interpretation, marked uncertain there. "Since" shows that the "if" is taken as true (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}; en {{deity_pronoun:sí|Sí}} mismo
decisions.reason: The stressed pronouns for the Son and for God take the setting; the clitic "lo" does not, as elsewhere in Spanish.

decisions.choice: el Hijo; con su propia gloria; muy pronto
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: ndani yake mwenyewe
decisions.reason: The meaning note: in God himself. "Ndani yake mwenyewe" (in himself) follows the Greek and the English; after "Mungu" as subject it points to God. Readable says "with his own glory", as the English does.

source.text: τεκνία, ἔτι μικρὸν μεθ’ ὑμῶν εἰμι· ζητήσετέ με, καὶ καθὼς εἶπον τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις ὅτι Ὅπου ἐγὼ ὑπάγω ὑμεῖς οὐ δύνασθε ἐλθεῖν, καὶ ὑμῖν λέγω ἄρτι.

records.literal_gloss: Little children, yet a little [while] with you I am; you will seek me, and just as I said to the Jews, 'Where I go you not are able to come,' also to you I say now.

en.L: Little children, yet a little [while] I am with you. You will seek {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and just as I said to the Jews, 'Where I go, you cannot come,' I also say to you now.
en.B: Little children, I am with you for only a short time more. You will search for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and what I said to the Jews I now say to you as well: 'You cannot come where I am going.'
en.R: My dear children, I will be with you just a little longer. You will look for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Earlier I told the Jews, 'You are not able to come where I am going.' Now I am telling you the same thing.

es.L: Hijitos, todavía un poco [de tiempo] estoy con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Me {{plural_you:buscarán|buscaréis}}, y como dije a los judíos: “Adonde yo voy, {{plural_you:ustedes no pueden|vosotros no podéis}} venir”, {{plural_you:también a ustedes se lo digo|también a vosotros os lo digo}} ahora.
es.B: Hijitos, estaré con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} solo un poco más de tiempo. Me {{plural_you:buscarán|buscaréis}}, y lo que les dije a los judíos ahora {{plural_you:se lo digo también a ustedes|os lo digo también a vosotros}}: “{{plural_you:Ustedes no pueden|Vosotros no podéis}} venir adonde yo voy”.
es.R: Hijos míos, estaré con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} solo un poco más. Me {{plural_you:buscarán|buscaréis}}. Antes les dije a los judíos: “{{plural_you:Ustedes no pueden|Vosotros no podéis}} venir adonde yo voy”. Ahora {{plural_you:les|os}} digo lo mismo a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

sw.L: Watoto wadogo, bado muda mfupi niko pamoja nanyi. Mtanitafuta, na kama vile nilivyowaambia Wayahudi, 'Mahali niendako {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, ninyi hamwezi kuja,' sasa nawaambia ninyi pia.
sw.B: Watoto wadogo, niko pamoja nanyi kwa muda mfupi tu zaidi. Mtanitafuta, na yale niliyowaambia Wayahudi nawaambia nanyi sasa: 'Hamwezi kuja mahali ninakokwenda.'
sw.R: Wanangu wapendwa, nitakuwa pamoja nanyi kwa muda mfupi tu zaidi. Mtanitafuta. Hapo awali niliwaambia Wayahudi, 'Hamwezi kuja mahali ninakokwenda.' Sasa nawaambia ninyi jambo hilo hilo.

decisions.choice: Little children: a tender address, as of a teacher or father to his own
decisions.reason: The word is a small, affectionate form of "children" and appears only here in this Gospel. The writer of 1 John uses it often for his readers (1 John 2:1, 12, 28; 3:7, 18; 4:4; 5:21). The word already takes in men and women.

decisions.choice: yet a little while: the short time left before his death and going away
decisions.reason: Jesus said the same to the crowds and the authorities (7:33; 12:35); he will say it again to the disciples (14:19; 16:16-19). The time is now a matter of hours.

decisions.choice: the Jews: those who heard him say this before (7:33-34; 8:21)
alternatives: the Jewish people as a whole
decisions.reason: Jesus points back to a particular occasion: the crowd and the authorities in the temple courts to whom he said these words (7:32-36; 8:21-22). The word John wrote is kept and tied to that occasion. Jesus and the disciples he is speaking to are Jews themselves.

decisions.choice: Where I go you cannot come: Jesus quotes his own words in 8:21 (and 7:34)
decisions.reason: The words are the same, but their meaning for the disciples differs. To his opponents Jesus added "you will die in your sin" (8:21). To the disciples he adds "now": they cannot come yet, but they will follow later (verse 36; 14:2-3).

decisions.choice: seek / search for / look for; Where I go, you cannot come (L); You cannot come where I am going (B); You are not able to come where I am going (R)
decisions.reason: The quotation keeps the English each level used in 8:21, and "seek" keeps the English of 7:34, so that readers can see that Jesus is repeating himself.

decisions.choice: My dear children; Earlier I told
decisions.reason: Readable gives the tenderness of the address in everyday words and says plainly that Jesus is pointing back to an earlier time.

decisions.choice: Adonde yo voy, ustedes no pueden venir
decisions.reason: Jesus quotes his own words, so Spanish uses the wording of 8:21 (meaning decision m4). "Los judíos" are those who heard him then (meaning decision m3), with no "dirigentes".

decisions.choice: Hijitos (L, B); Hijos míos (R)
decisions.reason: A tender address (meaning decision m1). "Hijitos" is warm, not childish, in Spanish.

decisions.choice: the words of 8:21 repeated: Mahali niendako mimi, ninyi hamwezi kuja (L); Hamwezi kuja mahali ninakokwenda (B, R)
decisions.reason: Jesus quotes what he said in 8:21 (and 7:34), so the quotation keeps the Swahili of 8:21 at each level. "Wayahudi" at every level, as at 8:22, for the people who heard him then.

decisions.choice: Watoto wadogo (L, B); Wanangu wapendwa (R)
decisions.reason: A tender address, as of a teacher to his pupils. Readable says "my dear children", as the English does.

source.text: ἐντολὴν καινὴν δίδωμι ὑμῖν ἵνα ἀγαπᾶτε ἀλλήλους, καθὼς ἠγάπησα ὑμᾶς ἵνα καὶ ὑμεῖς ἀγαπᾶτε ἀλλήλους.

records.literal_gloss: A commandment new I give to you, that you love one another; just as I loved you, that also you love one another.

en.L: A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another; just as I loved you, that you also love one another.
en.B: I am giving you a new commandment: love one another. In the same way that I have loved you, you too must love one another.
en.R: Here is a new commandment I am giving you: love each other. You must love each other the way I have loved you.

es.L: Un mandamiento nuevo {{plural_you:les|os}} doy: que {{plural_you:se amen|os améis}} unos a otros; como yo {{plural_you:los|os}} he amado, que también {{plural_you:ustedes se amen|vosotros os améis}} unos a otros.
es.B: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} doy un mandamiento nuevo: que {{plural_you:se amen|os améis}} unos a otros. Así como yo {{plural_you:los|os}} he amado, también {{plural_you:ustedes deben amarse|vosotros debéis amaros}} unos a otros.
es.R: Este es el mandamiento nuevo que {{plural_you:les|os}} doy: {{plural_you:ámense|amaos}} unos a otros. {{plural_you:Deben amarse|Debéis amaros}} unos a otros como yo {{plural_you:los|os}} he amado.

sw.L: Nawapa amri mpya, kwamba mpendane ninyi kwa ninyi; jinsi nilivyowapenda, ili ninyi pia mpendane.
sw.B: Ninawapa amri mpya: pendaneni. Kwa namna ile ile niliyowapenda, ninyi pia lazima mpendane.
sw.R: Hii ni amri mpya ninayowapa: mpendane. Mnapaswa kupendana jinsi nilivyowapenda.

decisions.choice: new: new in its measure, "as I have loved you"
alternatives: new because love for others had never been commanded before
decisions.reason: The Law already said "love your neighbor as yourself" (Leviticus 19:18). What is new is the standard and the source: the love Jesus has shown them, in washing their feet (13:1-15) and in laying down his life (15:12-13). 1 John 2:7-8 calls this commandment both old and new.

decisions.choice: just as I have loved you: both the pattern and the ground of their love
decisions.reason: "Just as" gives the measure of their love and also its reason: they love because he loved them first (compare 15:9, 12; 1 John 4:19). The past tense looks at his love as a whole, shown to the end (13:1).

decisions.choice: that you also love one another: the command repeated, now with its standard
alternatives: purpose: I loved you so that you too would love one another
decisions.reason: The second "that" most naturally repeats the content of the commandment. Read as purpose, it gives nearly the same sense: his love was meant to make them love.

decisions.choice: love one another (L, B); love each other (R); commandment
decisions.reason: "Love" is the book's word for this verb. The Greek leaves no other natural way to say "love one another"; the words around it are put freshly. Readable uses the plainer "each other".

decisions.choice: I am giving you a new commandment (B); Here is a new commandment I am giving you (R)
alternatives: A new commandment I give to you (Literal)
decisions.reason: The Greek puts "commandment new" first for weight. Balanced and Readable use the normal order and make the command itself a direct instruction, "love one another".

decisions.choice: mandamiento; amarse unos a otros
decisions.reason: The reflexive changes with the plural (se amen / os améis), so it sits inside the span.

source.text: ἐν τούτῳ γνώσονται πάντες ὅτι ἐμοὶ μαθηταί ἐστε, ἐὰν ἀγάπην ἔχητε ἐν ἀλλήλοις.

records.literal_gloss: By this will know all that to me disciples you are, if love you have among one another.

en.L: By this all will know that you are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} disciples, if you have love among one another."
en.B: If you have love for one another, everyone will know by this that you are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} disciples."
en.R: If you love each other, then everyone will know that you are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} disciples."

es.L: En esto conocerán todos que {{plural_you:son|sois}} mis discípulos, si {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} amor los unos por los otros».
es.B: Si {{plural_you:se aman|os amáis}} unos a otros, todos sabrán por esto que {{plural_you:son|sois}} mis discípulos».
es.R: Si {{plural_you:se aman|os amáis}} unos a otros, todo el mundo sabrá que {{plural_you:son|sois}} mis discípulos».

sw.L: Kwa hili wote watajua kwamba ninyi ni wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, ikiwa mna upendo kati yenu ninyi kwa ninyi."
sw.B: Mkiwa na upendo kwa kila mmoja, kwa hili kila mtu atajua kwamba ninyi ni wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}."
sw.R: Mkipendana, basi kila mtu atajua kwamba ninyi ni wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}."

decisions.choice: by this: points forward to the if-clause
alternatives: by this: pointing back to the commandment in verse 34
decisions.reason: "This" is explained by what follows: their love for one another is the mark by which people will know them.

decisions.choice: my disciples: disciples who belong to me
decisions.reason: Jesus uses an emphatic word for "my": not disciples of Moses (9:28) or of John the Baptist (1:35), but his.

decisions.choice: love among one another: love within the community of disciples
alternatives: love for all people in general
decisions.reason: The love meant is the disciples' love for each other, as in verse 34. Others see it from outside: it is visible to everyone. Compare 17:21, 23.

decisions.choice: the if-clause first (B, R); love each other (R)
alternatives: By this all will know ... if you have love (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the condition first so that "this" points to something already said. Readable turns "have love" into the verb "love", as in verse 34.

decisions.choice: the if-clause first (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English.

source.text: Λέγει αὐτῷ Σίμων Πέτρος· Κύριε, ποῦ ὑπάγεις;

records.literal_gloss: Says to him Simon Peter, "Lord, where are you going?"

en.L: Simon Peter says to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, where are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} going?"
en.B: Simon Peter asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, where are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} going?"
en.R: Simon Peter asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, where are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} going?"

decisions.choice: Lord: a disciple's address to his master
decisions.reason: Peter is one of the disciples who have come to believe (6:68-69), so the word is "Lord", as in 13:6, 9 and 13:13.

decisions.choice: where are you going: Peter takes up Jesus's "where I go" (verse 33)
decisions.reason: Peter passes over the commandment and asks about the going away. Jesus means his going to the Father through his death (7:33; 16:5, 28); Peter seems to think of a place he could go to as well (verse 37). The question comes again in 14:5 and 16:5.

decisions.choice: asked (B, R); says (L)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "asked" because Peter asks a question; the Greek verb is the ordinary "says", in the present tense, treated as in verse 31 (rendering decision r-en-1 there).

decisions.choice: Señor
decisions.reason: A disciple's address to his master (meaning decision m1); "Señor" at every level, as elsewhere in John.

source.text: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς· Ὅπου ὑπάγω οὐ δύνασαί μοι νῦν ἀκολουθῆσαι, ἀκολουθήσεις δὲ ὕστερον.

records.literal_gloss: Answered Jesus, "Where I go you are not able me now to follow, you will follow but later."

en.L: Jesus answered, "Where I go, you cannot follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} now, but you will follow later."
en.B: Jesus answered, "You cannot follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} now to the place where I am going, but later you will follow."
en.R: Jesus answered, "You are not able to follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} now to where I am going. But you will follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} later."

es.L: Jesús respondió: «Adonde yo voy, no me puedes seguir ahora, pero me seguirás más tarde».
es.B: Jesús le respondió: «Ahora no puedes seguirme adonde yo voy, pero más tarde me seguirás».
es.R: Jesús le respondió: «Ahora no puedes seguirme adonde yo voy. Pero más adelante me seguirás».

sw.L: Yesu akajibu, "Mahali niendako, huwezi sasa kunifuata, lakini baadaye utafuata."
sw.B: Yesu akajibu, "Huwezi kunifuata sasa kwenda mahali ninakokwenda, lakini baadaye utafuata."
sw.R: Yesu akajibu, "Huwezi kunifuata sasa kwenda ninakokwenda. Lakini utanifuata baadaye."

decisions.choice: now ... later: the stress falls on "now"
decisions.reason: Unlike the hearers of 8:21, Peter is not shut out for good. He cannot follow at this moment; he will follow afterward.

decisions.choice: you will follow later: Peter will follow Jesus in a death that glorifies God, and so to the Father
alternatives: you will follow me to the Father's house, without a reference to Peter's death
decisions.reason: John later tells how Jesus foretold the kind of death by which Peter would glorify God, and then said to him, "Follow me" (21:18-19). That suggests this saying already points to Peter's death. Following Jesus also means being where he is (12:26; 14:2-3), so both may be meant. The allusion is likely but not certain.

decisions.choice: follow: go after him as a disciple, sharing his path
decisions.reason: "Follow" is the word for discipleship from the first chapter (1:37-43) and includes going where he goes (12:26). Here Peter is told he cannot yet take the path Jesus is about to take.

decisions.choice: You cannot follow me now to the place where I am going (B); to where I am going (R)
alternatives: Where I go, you cannot follow me now (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable begin with the main clause, and Readable repeats "me" after the second "follow", which the Greek leaves understood.

decisions.choice: Ahora first (B, R)
decisions.reason: Puts the stress on "now" (meaning decision m1).

source.text: λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Πέτρος· Κύριε, διὰ τί οὐ δύναμαί σοι ἀκολουθῆσαι ἄρτι;

records.literal_gloss: Says to him the Peter, "Lord, why not am I able you to follow now?

en.L: Peter says to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, why can I not follow {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} now?
en.B: Peter said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, why can I not follow {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} right now?
en.R: Peter asked, "Lord, why am I not able to follow {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} right now?

es.L: Le dice Pedro: «Señor, ¿por qué no puedo seguirte ahora?
es.B: Pedro le dijo: «Señor, ¿por qué no puedo seguirte ahora mismo?
es.R: Pedro le preguntó: «Señor, ¿por qué no puedo seguirte ahora mismo?

sw.L: Petro anamwambia, "Bwana, kwa nini siwezi kukufuata sasa?
sw.B: Petro akamwambia, "Bwana, kwa nini siwezi kukufuata hivi sasa?
sw.R: Petro akauliza, "Bwana, kwa nini siwezi kukufuata sasa hivi?

decisions.choice: now: at this very moment
decisions.reason: Peter uses a word that means "right now", sharpening the "now" of verse 36. He will not accept a delay.

decisions.choice: why can I not: Peter hears "cannot" as a limit he can overcome by being willing
decisions.reason: Jesus spoke of what Peter is not yet able to do; Peter answers as if it were a matter of courage. His next words show what he thinks he is ready for.

decisions.choice: right now
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "right" to show that Peter's word for "now" is sharper than the one Jesus used (meaning decision m1). Readable drops "to him", which is clear from the context.

decisions.choice: ahora mismo
decisions.reason: As in English.

source.text: τὴν ψυχήν μου ὑπὲρ σοῦ θήσω.

records.literal_gloss: The life of me for you I will lay down."

en.L: I will lay down my life for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."
en.B: I will lay down my life for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."
en.R: I will give up my life for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}!"

decisions.choice: lay down my life: give up one's life by dying, freely
decisions.reason: It is the expression Jesus used of the good shepherd, who lays down his life for the sheep (10:11, 15, 17-18), and he will use it again of the greatest love (15:13). Peter offers to do for Jesus what Jesus is about to do for him.

decisions.choice: for: on behalf of
decisions.reason: The word means for the sake of and in defense of someone, as in 10:11 and 11:50-52.

decisions.choice: my life: put first for emphasis
decisions.reason: Peter puts "my life" at the head of the sentence: he is ready to give not less than everything.

decisions.choice: lay down my life (L, B); give up my life (R)
decisions.reason: The same English as 10:11-18 at each level, so that the echo of the good shepherd is heard, and so that Jesus's reply in verse 38 repeats Peter's words exactly. Literal follows English order rather than putting "my life" first (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: pondré (L); daré (B); entregaré (R) mi vida
decisions.reason: The same verbs as for the good shepherd at 10:11 and 10:17, so Peter's promise is heard against them (meaning decisions m1 and, in 13:38, m2). "Ti" for Jesus takes the setting.

decisions.choice: kuyatoa maisha (L, B); nitakufa (R)
decisions.reason: The words of 10:11, 15 and 17, where the good shepherd gives his life ("huyatoa maisha yake"), so the reader hears Peter offering what Jesus said he would do. "Maisha" for this word, as in 12:25. Readable says plainly "I will die for you"; verse 38 answers in the same words.

source.text: ἀποκρίνεται Ἰησοῦς· Τὴν ψυχήν σου ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ θήσεις;

records.literal_gloss: Answers Jesus, "The life of you for me will you lay down?

en.L: Jesus answers, "Your life for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} you will lay down?
en.B: Jesus answered, "Will you really lay down your life for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?
en.R: Jesus answered, "Will you really give up your life for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?

es.B: Jesús le respondió: «¿De verdad darás tu vida por {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}?
es.R: Jesús le respondió: «¿De verdad vas a entregar tu vida por {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}?

sw.L: Yesu anajibu, "Maisha yako kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} utayatoa?
sw.B: Yesu akajibu, "Kweli utayatoa maisha yako kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}?

decisions.choice: a question that hands Peter's words back to him, with doubt
alternatives: a plain question asking for information
decisions.reason: Jesus repeats Peter's sentence word for word, in the same order, turning it into a question. The next sentence shows that the question doubts the promise.

decisions.choice: the irony: it is Jesus who will lay down his life for Peter
decisions.reason: Peter offers to die for Jesus; in fact the good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep (10:11, 15), Peter among them. Peter's own offer will be made good later (21:18-19).

decisions.choice: really
alternatives: Will you lay down your life for me?
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "really" to carry the doubting tone that the repeated words have in Greek (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps the Greek order, which itself echoes Peter's.

decisions.choice: De verdad
decisions.reason: As in English; the same verbs as Peter's in verse 37.

source.text: ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω σοι, οὐ μὴ ἀλέκτωρ φωνήσῃ ἕως οὗ ἀρνήσῃ με τρίς.

records.literal_gloss: Truly truly I say to you, not not a rooster will crow until you will deny me three times."

en.L: Truly, truly I say to you, a rooster will by no means crow until you deny {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} three times."
en.B: Truly, truly, I tell you, no rooster will crow before you have denied {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} three times."
en.R: I tell you the truth: before a rooster crows, you will say three times that you have nothing to do with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

es.L: En verdad, en verdad te digo: no cantará el gallo sin que me hayas negado tres veces».
es.B: En verdad, en verdad te digo que no cantará el gallo antes de que me hayas negado tres veces».
es.R: Te digo la verdad: antes de que cante el gallo, dirás tres veces que no tienes nada que ver conmigo».

sw.L: Kweli kweli nakuambia, jogoo hatawika kamwe hadi uwe umenikana mara tatu."
sw.B: Kweli kweli nakuambia, hakuna jogoo atakayewika kabla hujanikana mara tatu."
sw.R: Nakuambia ukweli: kabla jogoo hajawika, utasema mara tatu kwamba huna uhusiano wowote {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}}."

decisions.choice: will by no means crow: a strong negative
decisions.reason: The Greek uses a doubled negative, the strongest way to say that something will not happen. The rooster will not crow before the denials are complete.

decisions.choice: the rooster's crow: a marker of the last part of the night
alternatives: a single rooster at a set moment
decisions.reason: Roosters crow in the small hours before dawn, and the watch of the night before dawn could be called "cockcrow" (Mark 13:35). Jesus means that it will happen this very night, before it ends. John tells it happening in 18:27.

decisions.choice: deny: disown, say that one does not belong to him
decisions.reason: Peter's denials in 18:17, 25-27 are denials that he is one of Jesus's disciples ("I am not"). He disowns Jesus, not a belief about him.

decisions.choice: Truly, truly I say to you (L); Truly, truly, I tell you (B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering for John (see 1:51), recorded once in this passage.

decisions.choice: before a rooster crows, you will say three times that you have nothing to do with me
alternatives: you will deny me three times
decisions.reason: Readable explains "deny" by what Peter will say (meaning decision m3) and puts the time first.

decisions.choice: En verdad, en verdad te digo (L, B); Te digo la verdad (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering, here in the singular, to Peter alone.

decisions.choice: dirás tres veces que no tienes nada que ver conmigo
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: Kweli kweli nakuambia (L, B); Nakuambia ukweli (R)
decisions.reason: Here Jesus speaks to Peter alone, so the singular "nakuambia", as at 3:3. Readable gives "deny" its sense, saying one has nothing to do with him.
